title: Product Seeding Software: How to Recruit, Ship and Measure at Scale
summary: See how product seeding software runs the full loop: find creators, control sample rules, ship from your store, and measure GMV per gifted unit.
body_markdown:
## The End-to-End Seeding Workflow: Six Stages With Guardrails


Run each sample through six stages, with a defined approval or status update at every handoff. This creates a sample funnel showing what is requested, moving, and due for follow-up. Set rules to match your inventory, campaign terms, and fulfillment capacity.


### Stage 1: Creator Discovery and Offer, AI Ranking and Personalized Outreach at Scale


Define creator fit before outreach: product category, content style, audience, and campaign goal. Reacher’s[AI Creator Search](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-discovery) supports searches by profile, transcript, visual, or lookalike creator. Outreach runs across DM, Target Collab, and email at up to 10,000 creators a day; personalized messages can be drafted with tone control and previewed before sending. State the offer plainly, including what the creator receives and whether content is requested.


### Stage 2: The Sample Queue, Self-Selection Rules, Item Caps, Basket Limits, and Restricted SKUs


Set eligibility and inventory rules before opening requests. Decide which products creators can select, how many items each person may request, and whether a weekly cap limits total approvals. Exclude restricted or low-stock SKUs, and establish criteria for accepting or declining requests. A queue with bulk rejection and status controls helps prevent one campaign from consuming stock intended for other channels.


### Stage 3: Fulfillment From Your Shopify Store With Shipping Notifications


Connect the sample workflow to the store catalog and fulfillment process so approved requests can move to packing and shipping with fewer manual handoffs. Confirm the selected SKU, recipient details, and available inventory before dispatch. Record shipment and delivery updates, and notify creators when to expect the package. Check catalog and shipping data before launch; the system cannot correct inaccurate product or address details on its own.


### Stage 4: Proof of Action, the Timestamped Sample Status Log


Give every sample a status that reflects the latest verified action: requested, approved, shipped, received, posted, or GMV recorded. Add timestamps and preserve transition history, so a team can distinguish a pending request from an overdue delivery or completed post. This record supports follow-up without requiring a manager to track every package personally.


Set an owner and next action for each unresolved status. A shipped sample with no delivery confirmation needs a fulfillment check; a received sample without content needs follow-up based on campaign terms. A consistent log helps separate process delays from creator decisions.


### Stage 5: Re-Engagement, Winning Back Declined and Unresponsive Creators


Not every eligible creator responds or accepts an offer. Use status and message history to distinguish a decline from silence, then close the request, adjust the offer, or re-engage when there is a clear reason. Reacher includes Re-engage tools for creators who stalled, allowing teams to work from existing records instead of rebuilding context from old messages.


### Stage 6: Conversion, From Gifted Creator to Affiliate Program and Spark Codes


When a creator posts and demonstrates product fit, invite them into the ongoing affiliate program with clear commission terms and next steps. Track activity beyond the initial sample, since repeat posting and sales can make a creator more valuable than a single campaign deliverable. Reacher’s[creator CRM](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-crm) tracks status, messages, samples, and GMV, while GMV Max automates Spark Codes and ad budget. Keep the progression visible: gifted, posted, affiliate, and ongoing performance.


### Sample Funnel: Pre-Launch Checklist


- Define creator fit, offer terms, and any posting expectations.
- Set request eligibility, weekly caps, item limits, and restricted products.
- Confirm catalog details, inventory availability, fulfillment ownership, and shipping updates.
- Assign sample statuses and follow-up owners before requests open.
- Decide how posted creators move into the affiliate program and ongoing measurement.
